business_scope.primary_industry_name: Operating and Financial Leasing of Turbofan Aircraft Engines

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-United States Income Tax Treaty (1996, as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
Luxembourg-France Double Taxation Agreement (1958, as amended)
Luxembourg-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (1967, as amended by subsequent protocols)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 13 February 2018 and the Law of 25 March 2020; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and its implementing Grand-Ducal Regulations; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 and CSSF Circular 18/698 on AML/CFT professional obligations; EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 on cash controls.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity card of each direct shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or civil registry authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for countries party to the Apostille Convention OR Consular Legalization by a Luxembourg embassy or consulate for non-Apostille jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or official extract from the commercial register of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial register or company registry of the corporate shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address for each shareholder, manager and UBO (recent utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin certifying the copy and the issuing utility provider or bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized beneficial owner declaration (form of declaration foreseen by the RBE rules) executed by the founding shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary for the authentic formation deed and any foreign notary for ancillary declarations of non-resident shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for foreign ancillary declarations

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and documentary evidence of the lawful source of formation capital and aviation engine lease funding
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution or regulated funding provider of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank-stamped document with notarized signature where required; Consular Legalization only if issued by an institution in a non-Apostille jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at onboarding and on a daily risk-sensitive basis against: (a) the Luxembourg consolidated list of targeted financial sanctions maintained by the Ministry of Finance and the Restrictive Measures Unit; (b) the European Union's consolidated financial sanctions lists adopted under the CFSP framework, including all EU Council Regulations applicable in Luxembourg; (c) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list and FATF public statements; (d) the OFAC SDN list and OFAC sectoral sanctions on a best-efforts risk-management basis because the aviation leasing business uses USD Swift Wire payment rails; and (e) domestic Luxembourg PEP registers and CSSF guidance on enhanced due diligence arising under CSSF Circular 18/698. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons, shareholders from high-risk third countries, and counterparties that are government-owned air carriers or defense-related lessees.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) electronic portal at https://www.lbr.lu for RCS name availability verification and filing; name clearance is requested through the notary as part of the single incorporation submission and may be pre-checked on the LBR name availability tool.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be composed in French, German or Luxembourgish and must be rendered in Latin script. The statutory legal form suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' must appear exactly in the articles of association and in the published notice. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name in Luxembourg, must not mislead as to the nature, legal form, nationality or public character of the company, and must comply with the spelling rules applicable to the chosen local language.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RCS name clearance is valid for 28 days from the date of the notary's submission; extensions are not granted at the RCS level, and if the incorporation deed is not filed and published within the reservation window, a new name reservation must be made and, where applicable, new notarial costs will arise. In the event of a rejection by the RCS name review unit, the applicant may within one month of notification file a written administrative re-examination request through the notary, attaching evidence of prior trademark rights, coexistence consents, or a remedial amendment of the proposed name. If the rejection is confirmed, an appeal may be lodged with the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg (Tribunal administratif) within three months of notification of the final administrative decision; alternatively, a fresh reservation under a modified name may be submitted through the LBR portal without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the sole statutory registered office (siège social) of a Luxembourg SARL. The company must maintain a genuine physical office presence in Luxembourg where the statutory books, accounting records, shareholders' register and board minutes are kept and where mail can be received by duly authorized persons. A serviced office or administrative agent arrangement may be acceptable only if supported by a genuine lease or service agreement, display of the company name, and substantive indicators such as the availability of premises, personnel, local decision-taking and engine lease management functions; these elements are decisive for Luxembourg tax residence and for the OECD and Luxembourg economic substance requirements applicable to an aviation dry-leasing vehicle.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium risk, estimated at 15 to 25 percent over the first 24 months of operation. The principal inspection triggers are Luxembourg tax substance reviews conducted by the Administration des contributions directes and the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, CSSF AML/CFT on-site inspections of the regulated corporate service provider, and RCS verification of the reality of the registered office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS name clearance and availability pre-verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory: no filing fee for name availability verification; costs are absorbed in the notarial incorporation fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation and drafting of the articles of association (statuts SARL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (Société des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Law of 9 December 1976 on notarial fees as amended; prevailing market benchmark of EUR 1,800 to EUR 2,500 for a standard SARL with two to five corporate or individual shareholders.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS and RESA
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: RCS filing fee approximately EUR 75 and RESA publication fee approximately EUR 50, plus any notarial runner fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE/UBO register) initial filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutorily free of charge for the initial filing made concurrently with the incorporation notification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization bundle for foreign corporate, identity, address and source-of-funds documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authorities in each country of origin and Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs for consular legalization where applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Luxembourg consular fee schedule (droit de légalisation) and foreign apostille fee schedules; aggregate estimate for four to six documents with two certified copies each.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified sworn translation of foreign formation documents, passports and corporate extracts into French, German or Luxembourgish
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator registered with the Luxembourg District Court (traducteur assermenté)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of approximately EUR 30 to EUR 50 per 100 words for sworn translations, calculated on the estimated total word count of the formation bundle.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and commercial substance address arrangement (physical seat service, first-year deposit)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Approved corporate service provider or regulated fiduciary subject to CSSF supervision
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg market benchmark for a physical office, meeting room access, mail handling and substance support; annualized deposit of EUR 2,600 to EUR 3,200.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT onboarding file, PEP and OFAC/UN/EU sanctions database screening and UBO risk assessment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance software provider and designated AML compliance officer (responsable) under the Law of 12 November 2004
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription benchmark for EU consolidated sanctions, UN consolidated sanctions, OFAC SDN and global PEP datasets, including the UBO risk scoring service for a medium-risk aviation leasing vehicle.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial accounting, substance file and aviation engine dry-leasing documentation support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified public accountant (expert-comptable) and legal counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for formation-phase substance documentation, including first board minutes, registered office confirmation, leasing platform set-up notes and engine asset pre-acceptance records.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account and escrow pre-opening KYC due diligence charge
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Credit institution or licensed escrow agent supporting Swift Wire and Escrow Account payment rails
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank published account onboarding tariff and escrow agent initial KYC review flat fee, excluding ongoing maintenance and wire fees.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Title V, Articles 710-1 to 710-27 (S.à r.l. regime); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the Annual Accounts (RCS Law), Articles 1-8; Law of 31 May 1999 on the fire and rescue service; Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of craft, commerce and industry (optional establishment authorization); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering (AML risk tier: Medium-Risk Enhanced).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Ministry of Justice; e-filing via the RCS Online portal at www.lbr.lu and the State portal www.guichet.lu; notarial oversight by the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) containing the articles of association (statuts), executed before a Luxembourg notary in French, filed electronically with the RCS by the notary within one month of execution, and published in the official electronic gazette RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations). Regulated notarial tariffs (approx. EUR 1,500-3,000) and bank charges are payable separately from the state fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000, fully subscribed; each part (share) must be paid up to at least 20% of its nominal value at incorporation (aggregate minimum EUR 2,400), deposited into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) in the name of the S.à r.l. en formation at a Luxembourg credit institution; the bank blocking certificate is provided to the notary and funds released only upon RCS registration. For aircraft-engine dry-leasing SPEs, full payment of the stated capital is market practice. The former EUR 1 simplified S.à r.l.-S regime has been abolished by the Law of 23 September 2020.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD (MANAGERS') RESOLUTION — Adopted unanimously in writing by the founding manager(s). RESOLVED: (1) the share subscriptions and capital contributions of EUR 12,000 are accepted, and escrowed funds released to the Company; (2) the registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; (3) [NAME] is appointed as Manager (Gérant), acting separately and without joint authorization; (4) bank mandates and signature rules for all Company accounts are established; (5) all incorporation expenses and notarial fees are approved. The Manager is authorized to complete filings with the Luxembourg Business Registers, tax authorities, and social security body.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) - Luxembourg direct tax administration, corporate income tax and net wealth tax; Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) - VAT, registration duties, excise and customs (including EORI issuance); Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) - business register; unified e-government portal: MyGuichet.lu (Guichet Unique) for company registration, VAT registration and annual declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SARL: (1) incorporation is completed before a Luxembourg notary and the coordinated articles of association are filed with the RCS through the Guichet Unique within one month; (2) the RCS issues the registration extract (extrait) confirming the RCS number (format B-xxxxxx); the national identification number (matricule) is automatically issued by the State IT Centre (CTIE); (3) the AEDT automatically allocates a Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits) where a taxable activity is declared; in the absence of automatic allocation, the entity files the standard VAT registration application (form n° 400 for EU/foreign entities or standard RCS-linked notification) via MyGuichet.lu; (4) the ACD activates the corporate income-tax and net-wealth-tax file upon RCS registration; all annual CIT, NWT and VAT returns are e-filed through the ACD/AEDT Extranet and MyGuichet.lu; (5) for customs and export operations, the SARL obtains an EORI number (LU + 8 digits) from the AEDT customs division before lodging any import or export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope - The SARL is a resident, opaque taxable company subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (17% federal rate), the 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT, municipal business tax (6.75% in Luxembourg City, aggregate headline burden approx. 24.94%), and net wealth tax (0.5%); worldwide income is taxable for residents with credit and treaty relief; no pass-through or transparent election is available for a SARL (it is also a per-se corporation for US check-the-box classification); no tax-exempt zone applies because Luxembourg is a unitary national jurisdiction without sub-national tax-distinction regimes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or transparent status is available for a SARL; the relevant statutory elections and regimes are: (i) the participation-exemption election for qualifying dividends and capital gains (10% holding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition price for dividends; 10% or EUR 6 million for capital gains plus a 12-month holding period, subject to the subject-to-tax test); (ii) the notional interest deduction (NID) on qualifying new equity; (iii) the IP box (80% partial exemption on net qualifying IP income, subject to the nexus ratio); (iv) VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) between related Luxembourg entities under Article 61 LVA; (v) ATAD 2 hybrid-mismatch rules are mandatory with no elective carve-outs except statutory matching adjustments; (vi) revaluation and depreciation elections under the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR) available within the annual CIT return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (Luxembourg VAT Act - Loi TVA), harmonised with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC, administered by the Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover ceiling for the small-business franchise exemption (Article 57 LVA; goods and services); EUR 10,000 threshold for intra-Community distance sales and cross-border e-services; VAT registration is compulsory from the first euro of taxable activity for B2B intra-Community services (reverse-charge supplies), for non-established taxable persons, and for any entity seeking input VAT recovery; a dry-leasing SARL is registered from inception in practice.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or continuous-transaction-control API regime exists in Luxembourg (no SdI/VeriFactu-style mandate); B2G e-invoicing is mandatory via the PEPPOL network (EN 16931 format) since 23 April 2022; B2B and B2C e-invoicing remain voluntary and interoperable; the EU VAT-in-the-Digital-Age (ViDA) framework will introduce structured e-invoicing and digital reporting requirements by 2030; all customs export declarations must be lodged electronically through the Union Customs Code systems via the AEDT customs e-portal (including the Export Control System - ECS with exit confirmation).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the EU are zero-rated at 0% (Article 45 LVA) if the physical export takes place within 90 days, is evidenced from Luxembourg/EU customs records, and is documented before the VAT return deadline; for aircraft-engine dry leasing the transaction is treated as a supply of services (hiring of moveable tangible property other than means of transport), so the place-of-supply rule (Article 58 LVA for B2B) applies: an EU lessee outside Luxembourg triggers reverse charge in the lessee's Member State (no Luxembourg VAT), a non-EU lessee results in no Luxembourg VAT (outside scope), and a Luxembourg-resident lessee is subject to 18% Luxembourg VAT; where the transaction is re-characterised as a supply of goods (engine sale or finance-lease transferring title), full 0% zero-rating requires a customs export declaration, physical exit proof, and invoice issued within the statutory export evidence window.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/ENS lodged via the UCC Export Control System)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing dispatch from Luxembourg/EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT payment evidence evidencing the contractual consideration
Lease agreement (operating dry lease, ISIC 5223) identifying engine serial numbers and lessee
Engine logbooks, handover and redelivery certificates
VIES/valid VAT registration proof of the lessee (EU B2B reverse-charge substantiation)
Customs exit confirmation (UCC Article 335 electronic exit messages)
EORI-LU number evidence for the exporting SARL
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reassess zero-rating or outside-scope treatment within the 3-year VAT limitation period (extended to 5 years where no return has been filed and up to 10 years in cases of fraud); retrospective clawback reinstates Luxembourg VAT at 18% plus default interest of 0.6% per month on arrears; administrative fines generally range from EUR 250 to EUR 12,500 per infringement, and fraudulent export zero-rating claims carry penal tax of up to triple the evaded amount, risk of criminal prosecution (fines and imprisonment), and suspension of the offender's fiscal good standing, invoicing and EORI/customs privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as eurosystem member; foreign exchange regulatory oversight is exercised at EU level through ECB monetary policy and EU capital-movement guarantees, while BCL/CSSF administer bank and AML supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg has no foreign exchange law restricting convertibility; capital and current account transactions are fully convertible for EUR and all convertible currencies. Profit remittance, dividends, loan repayments, and lease payments are unrestricted under EU free movement of capital (TFEU Articles 63-65), subject to tax compliance and AML/KYC verification. BCL statistical reporting obligations apply for cross-border payments to aid eurosystem balance-of-payments compilation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Luxembourg; dry-lease receivables may be held in contract currency or EUR. However, the SARL must report cross-border trade payments to its Luxembourg bank under BCL external-statistics rules, and any receipt from a sanctioned or high-risk jurisdiction may require documentation proving the underlying aircraft engine transaction before crediting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as primary treasury rail. Luxembourg-licensed EMIs and PIs can support pre-funded accounts and payment services for operating expenses, but most do not provide SWIFT direct membership, escrow-grade settlement, aircraft title-money handling, or large FX lines; non-EU digital EMI-only accounts are not adequate for an aviation asset-holding SARL and carry enhanced AML refusal risk under CSSF circulars.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not specifically required by Luxembourg statute for a standard SARL, yet the practical onboarding policy of first-tier banks commonly requires an in-person meeting with at least one authorised director/managing partner and the ultimate beneficial owner, or a locally admitted notary / lawyer under a power of attorney. Remote opening may be accepted for EU-resident shareholders, but non-EU ownership and aviation-leasing risk normally trigger a video-call KYC interview plus hardening by a Luxembourg counsel attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-transparent shareholder/UBO chain in non-EEA jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered excerpts and UBO register (if available), notarised declarations, corporate structure chart, 12-month source-of-funds statements of each 25%+ UBO, and Luxembourg counsel AML opinion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Airframe/engine valuation and trade provenance uncertainty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Engine serial number registration, technical log books, valuation report by IATA- or ASA-accredited appraiser, lease agreement and redelivery conditions, insurance certificates, and title/history chain evidence.

Luxembourg corporate tax residence certificate, board meeting minutes, real substance proof (office/lease agreement, local director and activity programme, intra-group transfer-pricing documentation, decision-making evidence).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or aviation-sector screening hits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU/OFSI/OFAC consolidated-list screening reports, explanation of name/similarity false positives with passport and official IDs, ultimate beneficial owners' full declarations, and transaction counterparty due-diligence files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk payment corridor or unexplained third-party payment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original invoices and contracts, proof of relationship with counterparties, transaction flowcharts and purpose declaration, sworn affidavit confirming no third-party shell routing, and audited annual accounts/trial balance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity subscription proceeds and shareholder loans (subordinated or ordinary) must be routed through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers to the SARL's dedicated account in a Luxembourg Tier-1 bank; the funds reference field must show the transaction purpose, operating agreements or board resolution number, and the ECB/BCL balance-of-payments category for direct-investment capital (e.g., 'equity capital injection' or 'intercompany financing'). The bank requires a notarised contribution/corporate resolution, proof of identity/source of assets, and confirmation that incoming funds do not breach sanctions/embargoes. For amounts exceeding prescribed BCL thresholds, the bank will report to BCL on behalf of the SARL; an incoming capital payment may be placed in a blocked escrow-capital sub-account pending completion of registration/requisite legal formalities.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Dry-lease distributions and trade payments (engine maintenance reserves, OEM purchase invoices, redelivery costs, lessee refunds, dividends and lender repayments) should be settled via SWIFT MT103 for single beneficiary payments and MT202 covers for bank-to-bank nostro transfers. For large repossession/reserve movements, an irrevocable documentary credit or standby letter of credit issued by an OECD-country bank and financed against the engine lease assignment can be used, but ordinary operating leases settle on clean T/T terms. Each outbound payment must be accompanied by a payment purpose code consistent with the export/lease reason, invoices, and BCL reporting requirements to permit clearing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts with a Luxembourg/EU credit institution to hedge USD lease receivables into EUR under standard ISDA/CSA documentation
FX swaps for periodic rolling of liquidity across USD/EUR/GBP funding accounts
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) where finance leases or debt facilities are denominated in USD while equity is funded in EUR
European-style FX options for downside protection on illiquid or exotic currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on lightly convertible or restricted Central-Asian/African currencies, subject to ISDA/CSA collateral and EMIR reporting/clearing thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate for Luxembourg City (tax year 2024/2025), comprising national CIT 15.00%, unemployment-fund surcharge 0.50%, and municipal business tax 9.44%; other communes apply differing municipal multipliers.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box (80% exemption on qualifying IP income); participation exemption (100% exemption of dividends and capital gains on qualifying participations of at least 10% or acquisition cost of at least EUR 1.2 million held at least 12 months); notional interest deduction regime; R&D and innovation tax credits; accelerated depreciation on leased turbofan aircraft engines.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward under Art. 114 LIR, subject to annual offset cap: losses may not reduce taxable income by more than EUR 30,000,000 plus 70% of taxable income exceeding EUR 30,000,000).
